conviction_note: Peer and channel evidence published since EL last spoke (Aug 19) leans mildly positive for the Sep quarter. The strongest piece is L'Oréal's Q3 on Oct 22: LFL +7.2%, Luxe +7%, North Asia +7.8%, travel retail back to growth with sell-in about +10%. China NBS cosmetics was +5.4% in September. Against that, the stock is +16% over 20 days and near its post-print high, the whisper ($0.60) sits well above consensus ($0.51-0.52), Hainan summer sell-out was only +4.1%, and the Middle East drag persists. That gives p_up 54 on a ~9% event move, so +0.7 scaled, close to the +0.6 sum of the findings. The real swing factor is whether management firms or raises the FY27 guide, where consensus sits low in the range, and the release is not knowable in advance.
bar: Q1 FY27 consensus EPS $0.51-0.52 and revenue $3.65B (+4.9% y/y). Two agreeing sources: Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/EL/earnings-forecasts and Earnings Whispers https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/EL/21346 (whisper $0.60). No Q1 company guide. The FY27 guide is organic +3-5%, adj op margin 12.7-13.5%, adj EPS $3.10-3.35, with H1 stronger than H2 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001001250/000100125026000038/elq4fy2026exhibit991.htm). FY27 Street EPS of $3.18 is in the lower half of that range, and $15.5B revenue is at its bottom.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 8.0M shares, about 2.2% of float, 3.7 days to cover, falling (Aug 19, 2026 settlement per the equibles aggregator https://equibles.com/stocks/el/shortinterest, via search snippet; no October figure found). Not crowded, so no squeeze mechanism. The 25d skew of -1.7 vol pts is mildly call-bid (balanced lean). The event-implied move is 9.17% (straddle 9.84%). Spot 106.69 is +16.0% over 20 days and -1.8% over 5 days, near the post-earnings high of $109.35. Earnings Whispers sentiment is 19.2% bullish against 6.5% a quarter earlier.

findings.finding: L'Oréal's Q3 2026, reported Oct 22 (after EL last spoke on Aug 19), beat: group LFL +7.2% (+7.7% adjusted) against about +5.9% expected, Luxe +7% (EUR 4.18bn), North Asia +7.8% with China the driver, and Asia travel retail back to growth with sell-in about +10% and sell-out low-to-mid single digits. EL's FY27 guide assumes higher H1 travel-retail shipments; this is the closest peer confirmation that the July-September channel allowed them. Consensus has EL revenue +4.9%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 (Oct 30, 2025): organic +3% beat a guide of down LSD-to-slightly-positive, travel retail improved, and the stock moved +0.26%. Q4 FY26 (Aug 19, 2026): organic +5% beat plus a raised margin guide, +16.3%. Reported-quarter beats alone have been damped; beats with a guide move have paid.
findings.why_not_priced: EL fell 1.8% over the five sessions after L'Oréal's beat, and consensus revenue ($3.65B, +4.9%) sits at the low end of what an H1-weighted 3-5% organic guide implies. If the read-through were priced, EL would have risen with L'Oréal and estimates would have moved up from the bottom of the guide.
findings.independence: Same event from a second outlet with the travel-retail sell-in/sell-out detail: https://moodiedavittreport.com/?p=486532 (Oct 26, 2026). One document, counted once.

findings.finding: China NBS: September 2026 cosmetics retail sales were RMB 39.0bn, +5.4% y/y (August +4.9%), and January-September +6.1%, while total retail grew only +1.1%. Mainland China is a growth line for EL (+7% organic in Q4 FY26), and the category is still growing mid-single digits through the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: China was named the driver of the Aug 2026 beat (+16.3%) and of the Q1 FY26 beat (+0.26%).
findings.why_not_priced: A public macro series that is probably largely priced. It is filed small as a proxy: it confirms the category did not roll over in Q3, which a stock already +16% in 20 days needs, but it adds little beyond that.
findings.independence: Proxy (category-level, not EL). The L'Oréal North Asia +7.8% in finding 1 points the same way and is a different source.

findings.finding: Hainan offshore duty-free sales over the summer vacation period were RMB 3.82bn, only +4.1% y/y, against +25.7% in Q1 2026 and on a weak Q3 2025 base (-2.7%). L'Oréal said mainland China travel retail 'remained a bit negative'. So the sell-out under EL's planned travel-retail shipment step-up was modest, which risks either a smaller shipment benefit or channel inventory questions on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Travel-retail inventory resets drove EL's large negative prints in 2024-early 2025 (e.g. -16.1% on Feb 4, 2025, from the baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The Q1 Hainan headline (+25.7%) is the one the market remembers. If the summer slowdown were priced, consensus would not lean on H1 travel-retail shipments as a driver, and the stock would not sit near its post-print high.
findings.independence: L'Oréal's comment that mainland China travel retail was 'a bit negative', https://moodiedavittreport.com/?p=486532, a different source pointing the same way.

findings.finding: The Middle East conflict was still hitting fragrance in Q3. Interparfums' CEO put it at about 1% of Q3 sales, and Interparfums' US sales fell $10M on delayed gift-set shipments. EL's own Q4 FY26 took about 1pt off consolidated growth and 2pts off EUKEM from the conflict; EL guided 'not material' for FY27, with EUKEM stronger in H2, implying the drag persists in Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 FY26 print absorbed a 1pt ME hit and still rose +16.3%, so the line was looked through when the guide improved.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and inside what the company already guided: EL told the market EUKEM recovers in H2. This is filed as a modest reported-quarter drag.
findings.independence: EL's own Q4 FY26 release quantified the drag: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001001250/000100125026000038/elq4fy2026exhibit991.htm

findings.finding: Puig's Q3 2026: LFL +5.6% (record Q3), makeup +16.1% (Charlotte Tilbury launches), fragrance +3.9%, and skincare negative for a second consecutive quarter. The prestige market was healthy in Q3, but fragrance growth decelerated and makeup share went to a competitor. EL makeup is guided to return to growth only for the full year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fragrance was EL's strongest category in the last prints (+13% Q1 FY26, +10% Q4 FY26).
findings.why_not_priced: A mixed peer print with no clear net direction for EL. It is filed near zero because it neither confirms nor refutes the bar.

findings.finding: The effective bar is above consensus. The Earnings Whispers whisper is $0.60 against a $0.51-0.52 consensus (+15%), its bullish sentiment rose to 19.2% from 6.5% a quarter earlier, and the stock is +16% since the Aug 19 print, within about 2.5% of its post-earnings high. A merely in-line beat to $0.55 may be sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 beat consensus by a wide margin (EPS $0.32 vs ~$0.17-0.20 expected; revenue $3.48B vs $3.38B) and the stock moved only +0.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement of what is priced, not of what is missed: the run-up and the whisper mean a consensus-level beat is already in the stock. Its value is against the long-leaning findings above. Short interest is only about 2.2% of float, so there is no squeeze offset.
findings.independence: Same document. The run-up is from the sealed baseline (run_up_20d_pct +16.0).

findings.finding: The company's own phasing says Q1 should run above the 3-5% FY organic guide. The FY27 release says growth is 'stronger in the first half', citing earlier launches, higher travel-retail shipments and a lower H1 FY26 travel-retail base, and Q1 FY26 organic was only +3%. Consensus revenue of $3.65B (+4.9%) is roughly what that phasing implies, so this lands inside guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 printed inside/just above its guided phasing, +0.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the company told the market to expect this. It is filed small because consensus revenue sits only at the guided phasing, not above it, which leaves modest room for an organic print of +5-6%.
findings.independence: The L'Oréal travel-retail sell-in +10% (finding 1) corroborates the shipment driver from a different source.

findings.finding: There is room for a guide firm or raise. FY27 Street EPS of $3.18 sits in the lower half of the $3.10-3.35 guide and Street revenue of $15.5B at the bottom of $15.5-15.8B, while the company already raised its margin range once (to 12.7-13.5% from a preliminary 12.5-13.0% in May). A Q1 above the phasing, with a China investor event on Nov 4, gives management a reason to at least reaffirm toward the upper half.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is what moved EL: +16.3% when the margin outlook was raised (Aug 2026), and -19.2% in Feb 2026 and -16.1% in Feb 2025 on outlook cuts. In Q1 FY26 the guide was only reaffirmed and the move was +0.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: If a raise were priced, FY27 consensus would sit at or above the guide midpoint ($3.22) rather than $3.18, and revenue estimates would not sit at the bottom of the range. EL has historically reaffirmed rather than raised at Q1, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: EL FY27 outlook doc showing the earlier margin raise: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001001250/000100125026000038/elq4fy2026exhibit991.htm

findings.finding: Coty guided its own Q1 FY27 (July-September) LFL revenue down low-to-mid single digits, with gross margin down 50-100bp, a weak prestige-fragrance and mass peer for the same quarter. The weakness is largely Coty-specific (license exits, its own reset).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed EL reaction to Coty read-throughs in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since Aug 19, so it is priced. It is filed near zero for completeness as an idiosyncratic peer.

outside_window.finding: EL will webcast a 'Capital Markets Experience: China Ecosystem Immersion' presentation on Nov 4, 2026, two days after the print and after the exit window. Management likely has an incentive to show China strength, but any new China targets land after the window closes.
Coty's fiscal Q1 FY27 results (last year Nov 5) and Interparfums' full Q3 results and call (Nov 4-5) come after the window.

baseline_tension: The mildly positive channel read agrees with the slightly call-bid skew (-1.7) but runs into a +16% 20-day run-up and an elevated whisper. That pushes p_up toward 50 (to 54 from about 57), and the stock's reaction will hinge on the FY27 guide, not on the reported quarter.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the L'Oréal read-through cut from +1.0 to +0.8, because EL bought a clean reported-quarter beat at only +0.26% in Q1 FY26 and only guide moves have paid. Not cut further, because the lessons file names 'a peer's print landing after the company last spoke' as a pattern that has worked.

Rule 7 (positioning): short interest checked (about 2.2% of float, 3.7 DTC, not crowded). The whisper/run-up positioning negative trimmed from -1.0 to -0.8, because the skew is mildly call-bid and does not support a strong negative.
Rule 6 (bar and window): the bar has two agreeing sources ($0.51-0.52 / $3.65B), so no cap. The Nov 4 China investor event and the Coty/Interparfums calls moved to outside_window.
Rule 5 (proxies): the China NBS and Hainan findings are kept small as proxies; the sums were unchanged otherwise (0.6 pre and post, since the two trims offset in the sum).
